title: The rail is a list now

text:
Reload the tab. The hour box is gone, the rail is one chronological list, and ordinary items are now one line.

**Measured, 1920 and 400:** 386 rows — 68 big at 86px, 318 compact at **16px**. No console errors at either width.

## Three things I found that the minion could not

It wrote everything and **could not run a single command** — its shell refuses `node`, `git`, even `node --check`. It said so plainly instead of claiming otherwise, which is why these were findable at all. I ran the proofs myself.

**1. I had broken the rail previews.** Sending card bodies through the markdown renderer leaked the source into every preview — you would have seen `## In flight — 1 **[safe-rollout](…)**` where a sentence belonged. The body and the preview read the same field, so anything the body learns to render, the preview has to learn to strip. Fixed.

**2. The empty white box was still there.** The minion's diagnosis was exactly right and its fix was in the wrong layer: the toast wears a `flex` utility class, and `@layer util` beats `@layer theme` no matter the specificity, so its `[hidden]` rule could never win. Measured it still drawing at 35px tall. Real fix was to drop the utility class and let the component own its display. Third time a util-layer class has silently beaten component CSS here.

**3. The huge vertical flow was a feature at a stale scale.** Not sloppiness — the rail spaces cards *by elapsed time*, half an em per minute. That was written when every row was a 90px card. With 16px rows, a quiet twelve minutes drew **93px of nothing above a 16px row**, and only three rows fit a screen. Rescaled: five now. If it reads too flat, the gentler alternative is named in the code.

## Also done

The **Now and Grid padding** you flagged this morning — the task I stopped never got to it. Both now take the default padding; grid cards start at x=266 instead of flush against your sidebar. The timeline's full bleed is untouched.

## One thing that is my fault, not the code's

A row is big when it is `needs-you` or the newest `focus` card. **I have been marking nearly every card as both**, so the top of your rail is all big rows and you cannot see the compaction where you actually look. Nothing to fix in the code — I need to stop doing that, and I will.
